english.title: Driver a vehicle vehicle carrying dangerous / pressurised goods danger signs on container not matching load carried

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) drove a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), on a road, namely **(..SPECIFY THE LOCATION..), carrying goods or equipment subject to the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CHARACTER OF THE GOODS / EQUIPMENT..), in a container when the danger signs displayed on that container as prescribed and in the manner required by regulation 5 did not correctly describe the load being carried in that **(..SPECIFY THE FAILURE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 5 of the Carriage of Dangerous Goods and Use of Transportable Pressure Equipment Regulations 2009 and section 33(1)(c) and (3) of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For further guidance see the prosecution guide.
(ii) In the first instance a prohibition notice under section 22 of the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 may be applied in accordance with current HSE policy . Failure to comply with that prohibition should result in prosecution. Care should however be taken to obtain evidence to prove that the operator in the interim period had not complied with and therefore discharged the prohibition notice.
(iii) Where there is evidence of multiple offences, blatant disregard of the regulations or there has been previous advice, prosecution should also be considered.
(iv) ADR 2009 section 5.3 refers.

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: A fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
